label: rem:spectral-decomposition-qvalue-interpretation
title: Torus knots on $\Sigma_4$ as a self-dual basis: why the $Q$-value decomposition is exact and terminates at degree $2$
html:
The torus knots embeddable on \Sigma_4 form a complete, self-dual basis for the regular representation of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q). The Q-value of beta decay is the spectral decomposition of the decay operator in this basis. The decomposition is exact and finite. It terminates at degree 2 because the embeddability bound on \Sigma_4 kills all higher jets.

The six embeddable torus knots on \Sigma_4

See Table 1.

Degree-1 knots are already encoded in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}} through distinct vertex weights (\mathfrak{p} {}^i\!\oplus_j \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n} {}^i\!\oplus_j \mathfrak{n}, \mathfrak{p} {}^i\!\oplus_j \mathfrak{n} — inter-particle Hopf links with crossing indices i, j), so F = 1 for shells 1–4. The active correction comes from degree-2 knots only.

Jet bundle structure

The knot operators form a jet bundle over the exceptional divisor chain of \Sigma_g. The jet index is the Gröbner--Shirshov class (the degree in the degree tower) of each torus knot.

See Table 2.

The jet decomposition is exact and finite. This finiteness arises not from truncation, but from the finite dimensionality of the regular representation of H_n(q) on \Sigma_g. Completeness follows from the self-duality \tau(r,s) \leftrightarrow \tau(s,r) and the Rosso–Jones expansion. Every irrep of H_n(q) is recoverable from the torus knot invariants. Consequently, the knots form a complete orthogonal basis under the Markov trace inner product.

Geometric interpretation

Each factor in Q reads geometrically:

See Table 3.

The ratio \hbar_q / \ln q = 0.9496 is the discretisation correction. The exceptional divisors are q-spaced (discrete), not e-spaced (continuous).

Shell correction proportions

The product \prod F(\tau, N) reduces to two categorically defined proportions for shells \geq 5 (N > 28):

Degree-2 shell factor (F_{\mathrm{deg2}}). For shells at degree 2 in the torus knot tower, the two embeddable degree-2 knots \tau(2,9) and \tau(3,4) contribute a Rosso--Jones weighted average:

  F_{\mathrm{deg2}}
  = \frac{
      J(\tau(2,9)) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\tau(2,9) \cdot \Delta_\beta)
    + J(\tau(3,4)) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\tau(3,4) \cdot \Delta_\beta)
    }{
      \bigl(J(\tau(2,9)) + J(\tau(3,4))\bigr)
      \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\Delta_\beta)
    }
  \approx 3.6844,

where J(\tau(r,s)) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash r} d_\lambda(q) \cdot \omega_\lambda^s is the Rosso--Jones invariant (the quantum-dimension weighted trace of the full twist on each irrep of H_r(q)), and \Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn} is the beta-decay difference operator. The Rosso--Jones weights are the canonical inner product on R(H_r(q)). Schur orthogonality forces this structure; they assign each degree-2 knot its Rosso--Jones invariant J(\tau) with zero fitting freedom.

At q = q_0, with the \mathfrak{sl}_2 quantum dimensions d_\lambda(q) = \prod_{\square}[2+c(\square)]_q/[h(\square)]_q (so d_{(1^3)} = 0), J(\tau(2,9)) \approx 7.3936 and J(\tau(3,4)) \approx 16.3851, giving \tau(3,4) approximately 2.216\times the weight of \tau(2,9). With these weights and the Markov traces at z = q^3/(q^2+1) — \mathrm{tr}_M(\tau(2,9)\cdot\Delta_\beta) \approx 0.89764, \mathrm{tr}_M(\tau(3,4)\cdot\Delta_\beta) \approx 0.91725, and \mathrm{tr}_M(\Delta_\beta) \approx 0.24730 (for \Delta_\beta = \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}) — the displayed ratio evaluates to F_{\mathrm{deg2}} \approx 3.6844 > 1, so it acts as an amplification rather than a suppression.

Kummer tower decomposition. The two degree-2 knots correspond to the prime factorisation of the Euler characteristic |\chi(A)| = 6 = 2 \times 3 through the Kummer tower filtration (Kummer filtration):

  • \tau(3,4) has s = 4 = 2^2. This is the \mu_2 branch of the Kummer tower (even/odd parity).
  • \tau(2,9) has s = 9 = 3^2. This is the \mu_3 branch (threefold symmetry).

The Chinese Remainder Theorem decomposition \mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z} produces exactly these two independent components. The Rosso--Jones weights are the quantum dimensions of the corresponding Kummer components. J(\tau(3,4)) > J(\tau(2,9)) because the \mu_2 component (parity) possesses a larger quantum dimension in the degree-2 representation ring than the \mu_3 component (threefold symmetry).

Pauli exclusion factor (F_{\mathrm{Pauli}}). For magic-number neutron shells (N \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}), the filled shell projects onto the alternating irrep (1^3) via the Young symmetrizer e_{(1^3)}:

  F_{\mathrm{Pauli}}
  = \frac{|\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{alt}}(\Delta_\beta)|}
         {|\mathrm{tr}(\Delta_\beta)|}
  = \frac{|\lambda_{\mathrm{alt}}|}{|\lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}|},

where \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{alt}} evaluates each Hecke word w with eigenvalue (-q^{-1})^{\ell(w)} (alternating channel) and \mathrm{tr} uses q^{\ell(w)} (symmetric channel). This evaluates the ratio of alternating to symmetric eigenvalues of \Delta_\beta in the 6 \times 6 regular representation of H_3(q). These character evaluations do not involve the Markov parameter. For \Delta_\beta = \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} both characters equal 1, so this character ratio equals 1, whereas the Markov-trace Pauli quotient in part (iii) of the corollary vanishes identically at z = q^3/(q^2+1) because y_{(1^3)} = 0.

Combined formula. For a \beta^- decay with the converting neutron in shell degree d and neutron occupation parity p:

  Q
  = \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}}
    \times F_{\mathrm{deg2}}^{[d \geq 2]}
    \times F_{\mathrm{Pauli}}^{[N \in \mathrm{magic}]},

where [\cdot] is the Iverson bracket. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), F_{\mathrm{deg2}} \approx 3.6844 and the Markov-trace Pauli factor vanishes on filled shells (such as {}^{137}\mathrm{Cs} with N = 82).

Benchmark Q-values at z = q^3/(q^2+1)

The bare term and the combined formula, evaluated at the proton-anchored q_0 with z = q^3/(q^2+1), the normalisation |\log_q(P_{\mathrm{dau}}/P_{\mathrm{par}})|\cdot\hbar_q\cdot m_e/3 of the corollary, and nucleons ordered protons first (F_{\mathrm{deg2}} \approx 3.6844 applied for converting-neutron shells \geq 5; for {}^{137}\mathrm{Cs} at N = 82, the Markov-trace Pauli factor gives 0). {}^{3}\mathrm{H} (N = 2) and {}^{14}\mathrm{C} (N = 8) also fill a shell, but lie in shells 1–4, where F = 1; read literally, part (iii) of the corollary would give Q = 0 for them as well.

The bare term misses by 8–98\% and the combined formula by 1–100\%. The single close entry ({}^{60}\mathrm{Co}) sits among misses of tens of percent on both sides and is not evidence for the formula. The same computation reproduces Table 1 and the values of J and F_{\mathrm{deg2}} above.

Error structure

Let \varepsilon = \delta q / q \approx 1.2 \times 10^{-8} (CODATA). The parametric error is O(\varepsilon), which is negligible. The structural errors are O(1) relative to \varepsilon: at z = q^3/(q^2+1) they are 8–98\% for \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}} and 1–100\% for the combined formula (table above), arising from nucleon ordering in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}}, degree-2 Rosso--Jones weighting over two knots, degree-tower truncation, and the vanishing of the (1^3) Pauli branch. Whether the decomposition is complete is a separate claim; these residuals do not test it.
